demand.question: What is a VPC in one sentence: a logically isolated virtual network dedicated to one AWS account, living in one Region, and what you define inside it (IP range, subnets, gateways, security groups)?
How many Availability Zones does every Region have at least, and what is the difference between an AZ code (us-east-2a) and an AZ ID (use2-az1) across accounts?
demand.note: Source footnote: newer accounts can access two Availability Zones in US West (N. California); accounts created from November 2025 get a uniform code mapping in the oldest Regions.

demand.question: Does a VPC span all Availability Zones of its Region, and must a subnet reside entirely within one Availability Zone (cannot span zones)?
FAQ: Can a VPC span multiple Availability Zones? Can a subnet span Availability Zones? How do I determine which AZ my subnet is in?
demand.note: The FAQ answer 'Yes.' to 'Can a VPC span multiple AZs?' is too short to quote; vpc-spans-all-azs-in-region carries it. vpc-faq-subnet-single-az was merged into vpc-subnet-single-az by the registrar.

demand.question: Why launch resources in at least two Availability Zones (protect from the failure of a single zone), as the VPC guide and the Well-Architected reliability pillar state it?
What are AWS Local Zones, Wavelength Zones and Outposts from the VPC's point of view: a VPC extends to them with subnets; which gateway types apply (carrier gateway, local gateway)?
demand.note: keep short: one subsection pointer; chapter 02 owns the global infrastructure

demand.question: Does traffic between two instances in the same Region that use public IP addresses stay on the AWS private global network, and is it still billed as Regional data transfer?
demand.note: Registrar: the billing half was found by a targeted search in the EC2 FAQ (Availability Zones section) and added as vpc-data-transfer-public-ip-regional-rate: public or Elastic IP addresses get Regional Data Transfer rates even in the same AZ; charged once even if cross-AZ too.

demand.question: What does a default VPC contain: CIDR 172.31.0.0/16, a /20 default subnet in each AZ, an internet gateway, a main route table with 0.0.0.0/0 to the internet gateway, default security group, default network ACL, DHCP options?
Do instances launched into a default subnet receive a public IPv4 address and public DNS hostname by default, and do instances in a nondefault subnet (of any VPC) receive one?
Can you delete a default VPC, recreate one, and how many default VPCs can an account have per Region (FAQ and guide)?
What do the two VPC DNS attributes do (enableDnsSupport, enableDnsHostnames), what are their defaults for a default VPC versus a VPC you create, and must both be enabled for public DNS hostnames?
Where is the Amazon DNS server (Route 53 Resolver) reachable from a VPC: the VPC network range plus two, and 169.254.169.253?
What is a DHCP option set, what does AmazonProvidedDNS mean, can a VPC have more than one at a time, and can an option set be modified after creation (or must you create a new one)?
What IPv4 CIDR sizes can a VPC have: between /16 (65,536 addresses) and /28 (16 addresses)?
What IPv4 CIDR sizes can a subnet have (/28 to /16), must a subnet CIDR fall within the VPC CIDR, and may subnet CIDRs overlap?

Which five IP addresses in every subnet are reserved (first four and last), what is each used for (network, VPC router, DNS, future use, broadcast), and how many usable addresses does a /24 subnet have?
demand.note: 251 usable in a /24 is derived (needs a derive vote). The role of the first (network) address is only in a 3-word list item, so the claim names the other four roles.

demand.question: Which address ranges does AWS recommend for a VPC (RFC 1918 private ranges), is a publicly routable range allowed, and what about 100.64.0.0/10?
demand.note: Registrar: 100.64.0.0/10 found by a targeted search in the association-restrictions table of vpc-cidr-blocks; row adopted as vpc-secondary-cidr-restrictions-10-range (other rows of that table can be adopted the same way if a writer needs them).

demand.question: Can the primary IPv4 CIDR of a VPC be changed after creation, and can secondary CIDR blocks be added later; what restrictions apply to secondary CIDRs (no overlap with existing CIDRs or routes, allowed ranges relative to the primary)?
demand.note: The FAQ facts that said 'four secondary CIDRs' (fixed) were rejected as older wording; the quota is 5 IPv4 CIDR blocks by default, adjustable to 50.

demand.question: VPC quotas: VPCs per Region (5), subnets per VPC (200), IPv4 CIDR blocks per VPC (5, up to 50), IPv6 CIDR blocks per VPC (5), and the note that raising the VPC quota raises the internet gateway quota.

How should you plan CIDR ranges for growth: non-overlapping ranges across VPCs and on-premises networks, room for more subnets and AZs, and IPAM for allocation across accounts (Well-Architected reliability pillar and the VPC planning page)?

What is the difference between a private IPv4 address, a public IPv4 address and an Elastic IP address: which one is released when an instance stops, which one is static, and how many Elastic IPs per Region by default (5)?
Are public IPv4 addresses charged (every public IPv4 address, including Elastic IPs associated with running instances), since when (2024-02-01), and what does the pricing page say per IP-hour?
demand.note: FRESHNESS hypothesis confirmed: 'an attached EIP is free' is wrong since 2024-02-01. Adjudicate-10 (2026-10-12): vpc-public-ipv4-charge-2024 now notes the separate rate of the Amazon-provided contiguous IPv4 block; vpc-public-ipv4-free-tier-750-hours follows the current VPC guide (no '12 months'; a currency vote found that framing outdated). Both await fresh votes. close-facts-10 (2026-10-12): vpc-public-ipv4-free-tier-750-hours rejected after the second vote (currency outdated: since 2025-07-15 new accounts get a credit-based Free Tier; entail partial: no per-month period). The charge itself is grounded by the remaining facts; do not state a Free Tier allowance.

demand.question: What does the subnet attribute 'auto-assign public IPv4 address' do, and what is its default for a nondefault subnet?
What is a managed prefix list (customer-managed and AWS-managed), where can it be referenced (security group rules, route tables), and how do its entries count toward the rule quota?
What is Network Address Usage (NAU), what is the default NAU quota per VPC (64,000, adjustable to 256,000) and for peered VPCs (128,000), and what counts as one unit?
What is a subnet CIDR reservation and when would you use one?

demand.question: What is Amazon VPC IPAM, what does the free tier cover versus the advanced tier (multi-Region, multi-account, private IPv4 management), and what is the advanced-tier price per active IP address per hour?
FAQ: What is BYOIP, and what is the most specific IPv4 prefix you can bring (/24)?

Are Elastic IP addresses supported for IPv6 (no), and why does an IPv6 address not need one?

What is the difference between a dual-stack subnet and an IPv6-only subnet, which link-local IPv4 range do IPv6-only resources get (169.254.0.0/16), and how do DNS64 and NAT64 on a NAT gateway let IPv6-only resources reach IPv4-only services?

demand.note: Not found: no saved AWS page states the date 2023-11-16 verbatim (What's New post blocked by robots.txt; IPAM doc history fetched empty). demand.question: What makes a subnet public, private or VPN-only: the route table's route to an internet gateway, a NAT device, or a virtual private gateway (the guide's subnet types)?

What does an instance need to communicate with the internet: an internet gateway attached to the VPC, a route 0.0.0.0/0 to it, a public IPv4 or Elastic IP, and security group and network ACL rules that allow the traffic?

What is the standard multi-tier layout: public subnets for load balancers and NAT gateways, private subnets for application servers, private subnets for databases, repeated in at least two Availability Zones (the guide's web-and-database example)?
Where does a database belong (a private subnet with no route to the internet gateway), and how do administrators reach it without a bastion host (point to Session Manager in chapter 38)?
When is a single-AZ, public-subnet VPC acceptable (development or test environment), and why not for production?
What does the VPC planning page recommend for subnet sizing and future growth: subnets larger than needed, one subnet per tier per AZ, and leaving CIDR space for new AZs and VPCs?
demand.note: The guidance sits in Well-Architected REL02-BP03; 'one subnet per tier per AZ' is supported only through the examples (vpc-example-web-db-two-tier-layout), not as an explicit rule.

demand.note: 'without sending packets' is not said in those words; the guide says 'static configuration analysis tool'.

demand.question: What is the VPC resource map and the 'VPC and more' creation workflow, and what resources does it create (subnets, route tables, internet gateway, NAT gateways, S3 gateway endpoint)?

What is the local route: added automatically for the VPC CIDR, cannot be deleted, and can only be replaced to point at a network interface or Gateway Load Balancer endpoint (middlebox)?
How is a route chosen: longest prefix match first; when prefixes are equal, what is the priority order between local, static and propagated routes?

What can a route target be (internet gateway, NAT gateway, egress-only internet gateway, virtual private gateway, peering connection, transit gateway, gateway VPC endpoint, network interface, carrier gateway, local gateway), and which destination type each route type uses?
Route table quotas: route tables per VPC (200), routes per route table (500, up to 1,000), propagated routes per table (100).

What is a gateway route table (ingress routing): associating a route table with an internet gateway or virtual private gateway to send incoming traffic through a security appliance before it reaches a subnet.

demand.question: What routes make a subnet public for IPv6 (::/0 to the internet gateway) and private with outbound only (::/0 to an egress-only internet gateway)?

How does a route to a gateway endpoint look (destination is the service's managed prefix list, target is the endpoint), and why does a more specific route beat the 0.0.0.0/0 route to the NAT gateway?
What does route propagation from a virtual private gateway do, and what is the quota for propagated routes (100)?

demand.question: Where do you look first when an instance cannot reach a destination (the troubleshooting order: route table, security group, network ACL, public IP, internet gateway)?
demand.note: AWS gives no ordered troubleshooting checklist; the order is a teaching choice (label it as such), each step grounded in the listed facts. Looked in route-table-routes-troubleshoot, nat-gateway-troubleshooting, VPC_Internet_Gateway, custom-network-acl.

demand.question: What is an internet gateway: horizontally scaled, redundant and highly available, imposes no bandwidth constraints, no charge, and only one can be attached to a VPC at a time?

How does an internet gateway translate addresses: one-to-one NAT between the instance's private IPv4 and its public or Elastic IPv4; the instance only knows its private address; for IPv6 no translation.
Internet gateway quotas: 5 per Region, raised together with the VPC quota; egress-only internet gateways 5 per Region.

What is a NAT gateway for (instances in a private subnet connect out to the internet or other services; nothing can initiate a connection to them), and what are the two connectivity types: public (Elastic IP, public subnet, route through the internet gateway) and private (other VPCs or on-premises, no internet gateway)?
demand.note: Registrar: zonal-only facts (public subnet placement, one AZ, per-AZ deployment, 8 IP addresses) now carry a 'zonal NAT gateway' condition; Regional NAT gateways need no public subnet (d070).

demand.question: Is a NAT gateway tied to one Availability Zone, what happens to instances in other AZs that route through it if that AZ fails, and what does AWS recommend (a NAT gateway in each AZ, with each subnet routing to the NAT gateway in its own AZ)?

NAT gateway capacity: 5 Gbps scaling to 100 Gbps, 10 million packets per second, 55,000 simultaneous connections to each unique destination per IP address, up to 8 IP addresses on a zonal NAT gateway, and what to do when you need more (split subnets, add addresses).
demand.note: Adjudicate-10 (2026-10-12): the bandwidth and packet figures are scoped to zonal NAT gateways (no saved page gives them for regional NAT gateways); the 8-address limit is zonal, regional is 32 per AZ. Facts await fresh votes.

demand.question: Can a security group be associated with a NAT gateway (no; use security groups on the instances behind it), and does the network ACL of the NAT gateway's subnet apply to its traffic?
Which protocols does a NAT gateway support (TCP, UDP, ICMP), does it support port forwarding, what is its MTU (8500, since 2024-09-10), and does it fragment packets?

NAT gateway versus NAT instance, row by row: availability, bandwidth, maintenance, performance, cost, type and size, public IP, private IP, security groups, network ACLs, flow logs, port forwarding, bastion server, traffic metrics, timeout behavior, IP fragmentation.
demand.note: Private IP row says 'automatically selected'; registrar added the condition pointing to vpc-nat-private-ip-choice-change (you can choose it since 2022-11-17).

demand.question: What must you do to make an EC2 instance work as a NAT instance (disable source/destination checks, public subnet, Elastic IP, security group that allows the private subnets), and why is it a single point of failure?

What are the NAT gateway pricing dimensions: a charge per NAT Gateway-hour while provisioned and available, a data processing charge per GB regardless of direction, standard data transfer charges on top, partial hours billed as full hours; and the US East (Ohio) example rates ($0.045 per hour, $0.045 per GB).

How do you reduce NAT gateway charges: a gateway endpoint for S3 and DynamoDB (no hourly or data processing charge), keeping the NAT gateway in the same AZ as the instances to avoid cross-AZ data transfer, and more specific routes for private destinations.

What is a Regional NAT gateway (2025-11-19): one NAT gateway that expands and contracts across AZs with your workload, needs no public subnet, takes up to 60 minutes to expand to a new AZ, supports 32 IP addresses per AZ (zonal: 8), does not support private NAT, is not supported in constrained AZs; automatic versus manual mode.
demand.note: FRESHNESS hypothesis confirmed, including 'not supported in constrained Availability Zones'; GA 2025-11-19, examinable; older questions assume zonal only.

demand.question: How is a Regional NAT gateway billed: one NAT Gateway-hour for every AZ in which it is configured (three AZs for one hour = three hours), data processing per GB as before; compare the cost of three zonal NAT gateways with one Regional NAT gateway across three AZs.
demand.note: Three zonal NAT gateways (3 x $0.045 per hour) and one Regional NAT gateway across three AZs ($0.135 per hour) cost the same per hour in the Ohio example.

demand.question: NAT gateway quotas: 5 per Availability Zone (pending, active and deleting states count), 2 Elastic IPs per public NAT gateway (up to 8), 8 private IP addresses per NAT gateway.
What does the ErrorPortAllocation metric mean, what is the NAT gateway idle connection timeout (350 seconds), and how do secondary IP addresses raise the connection limit?

Which CloudWatch metrics does a NAT gateway publish (ErrorPortAllocation, PacketsDropCount, BytesOutToDestination, BytesOutToSource, ConnectionAttemptCount, ActiveConnectionCount), and at what interval?
When do you use a private NAT gateway: to reach another VPC or an on-premises network whose address range overlaps or that only accepts a specific source range (the guide's use cases).

Centralized egress through NAT gateways in a shared egress VPC behind a transit gateway versus a NAT gateway in every VPC: what does the multi-VPC whitepaper say about the cost and management trade-off?
demand.note: Go deeper; transit gateway itself is chapter 11

demand.question: What changed for NAT gateway addressing: secondary private IPv4 addresses (2023-01-31) and more Elastic IPs per public NAT gateway raise the ports available per destination (55,000 per address).

Which networking components are single points of failure and what removes them: one NAT gateway for all AZs (one per AZ or Regional), a NAT instance (NAT gateway), one subnet in one AZ (subnets in two or three AZs); which ones are already redundant (internet gateway).
What does the VPC resilience page say about Regions, Availability Zones and the managed VPC components?
demand.note: The resilience page talks about Regions and AZs only; it says nothing specific about managed VPC components.

demand.question: What is a security group: a stateful virtual firewall at the network interface (instance) level, allow rules only, all rules evaluated before deciding, and response traffic allowed regardless of inbound rules.

What are the rules of the default security group: inbound allows traffic only from resources in the same security group, outbound allows all; and what happens when you launch an instance without naming a security group?
What rules does a newly created custom security group have (no inbound rule; one outbound rule allowing all traffic)?

What can be the source or destination of a security group rule (an IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR, a prefix list, or another security group's ID), and what does referencing another security group allow (traffic from resources associated with it, not its rules)?

Security group quotas: 2,500 per Region, 60 inbound and 60 outbound rules per group (IPv4 and IPv6 counted separately), 5 security groups per network interface (up to 16), and the product that cannot exceed 1,000.
Do security group changes apply immediately to every associated resource, and what is connection tracking (which flows are tracked and when an existing connection is cut by a rule change)?

demand.question: Can a security group be used only in the VPC it was created in; since 2024-10-30, can a security group be associated with multiple VPCs in the same Region and shared across AWS Organizations, and what are the exclusions (default security groups, default VPCs)?
